rules: R1. scripts/ stays FLAT. Lifetime is recorded in scripts/README.md, never in the directory tree. Reason: all 25 Python scripts compute the repository root as Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], so any subdirectory breaks every one of them.

R2. A study script's name carries its subject, and its work item is stated in the first line of its docstring. Every script already does the second; the plan does not rename any file to satisfy the first.

R3. Test files are tests/test_<subject>.py. Claim-shaped names (test_gru_beats_baselines_on_fixture.py) are permitted where the test IS the claim, because renaming them would break pytest node ids cited in documents.

R4. runs/ artifacts are <task>/<detector>/<ISO8601-basic-Z>-<8-hex-digest>.json for a scored run, and <task>/_<study>/<ISO8601-basic-Z>-<label>.json for a study. Weights are runs/_weights/<32-hex-digest>.npz. This is what the tree already does; the rule is written down because it was never stated.

R5. Documents NEVER wrap a citable token across a line break -- a runs/ path, a repository path, a section number or a count. Measured cost of breaking this: 8 of 77 cited runs/ paths are unresolvable as written purely because of a line break, and docs/STATUS.md's stale test count is invisible to its own guard for the same reason.
R6. A generated document says so in its footer AND cannot be regenerated over hand-authored content. docs/DATA.md says so and can be; that is fixed rather than restated.
R7. A section number, once published, is never renumbered. It is the citation target for 629 cross-references.
R8. src/sentinel_* module names describe the artifact, not the experiment. No rename is proposed: the cost exceeds the gain while the import graph and the layering test depend on them.
